newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise in follow-through from Friday.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise in follow-through from Friday.

text.p: Stocks took a baby step higher Monday after Friday's rally but the market lacked the conviction it showed at the end of last week.

Just after 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 23.47 points to 7,024.36. The 30-share Dow jumped 56 points on Friday, boosted by the government's report of strong job growth in February with little upward pressure on wages.

In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a 13-10 margin on moderate volume of about 202 million shares. The Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-technology issues, added 6.61 points to 1,318.41.

"What we are seeing are the remnants of last week's strength. But there is more caution and less exuberance today than we saw on Friday," said Hugh Johsnon, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

"Transports and utilities have come in for some profit-taking and the groups that are leading the market higher -- tobacco, drugs, foods -- are defensive. And large companies are doing better than small ones. That tells you that investors are worried and cautious."

Investors remain worried about Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warnings that stocks could be overvalued and that the central bank might raise short-term interest rates. The next meeting of Fed policy-makers is set for March 25.

"Wall Street takes Alan Greenspan seriously, even if his remarks are ambiguous," Johnson said. "When he says that stocks may be overvalued and caution is warranted, his words are taken seriously. Every savvy investor agrees with Greenspan that history councils caution."
The bond market provided little support. The 30-year Treasury lost nearly a quarter point, or $2.50 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.83 percent from 6.82 percent on Friday.
Among Dow issues, Philp Morris added 1-1/4 to 137-1/4, Merck rose 1-1/4 to 94-1/4 and Procter & Gamble jumped 3-3/4 to 124-1/4.

The Nasdaq market drew some strength from Intel, up 1-1/8 at 144-5/8 in active trading. Cisco Systems lost 1-1/4 to 50-1/8. PaineWebber downgraded the maker of computer network equipment to neutral from buy, traders said.
"The techs are under pressure, even though some of them are doing well today," Johnson said. "They just ain't as cheap as they were in '95 and '96."
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks added 1.99 points to 806.96.
The American Stock Exchange index gained 0.47 point to 602.53.
